# OverheardCoach: an on-device real-time social-situation interpreter for autistic and socially-anxious adults
**Claim:** Sub_category: Accessibility (Vision/Hearing/Speech/Motor) → social-cognition accessibility. An app running on-device multimodal models that listens to a live in-person conversation (with consent settings) and gives the user discreet real-time private cues — detected sarcasm, implied questions they should answer, when they are dominating/interrupting, tone mismatches — via a watch tap or one-line glanceable prompt, for neurodivergent and socially-anxious adults.
**Mechanism / rationale:** Depends on (1) on-device multimodal models (Gemini Nano with audio, Apple Intelligence local audio models [developer.android.com][touchzen.ai]) that transcribe and reason over speech locally for privacy, and (2) real-time low-latency voice/audio pipelines now at 90-307ms P50 [assemblyai.com]. Both are load-bearing: shipping raw conversation audio to the cloud is a privacy non-starter for intimate social settings, and a year ago on-device models could not do multimodal pragmatic/tone inference locally — only cloud models could, which the use case forbids. Revenue path: ~5.4M US autistic adults + tens of millions with social anxiety; reachable beachhead ~3M via clinician/advocacy channels, 1% = 30,000 at $12/mo → $4.3M/yr.
**Novelty:** Closest competitors — Yoodli, Tough Tongue [yoodli.ai] — do offline *practice* roleplay, not live in-situ assistance; accessibility apps (Seeing AI, Be My Eyes [atandme.com]) handle vision, not social pragmatics. White space: nobody offers real-time, on-device, privacy-preserving *live* social-pragmatic coaching during actual conversations.
**Test:** Lab study with 30 autistic adults using the app in scripted then naturalistic conversations; measure self-reported confidence, third-party rated conversational reciprocity, and cue precision/recall against human-coded transcripts. Refute if cue precision <70% or users find latency disruptive.
**Assumptions:** On-device models can infer pragmatics/sarcasm at usable accuracy; one-party-consent recording is legally/ethically framed; glanceable cues don't increase cognitive load mid-conversation.
